newsitem.title: POLAND: OFFERS IN PROCHNIK TENDER REDUCED 22 PCT.
newsitem.headline: OFFERS IN PROCHNIK TENDER REDUCED 22 PCT.

text.p: Investors selling Polish garment maker Prochnik SA shares in the tender offer called by National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 12 had offers reduced by 21.75 percent, an official of the brokerage running the tender said.
In February NFI 12 announced a public tender offer to buy 343,501 Prochnik shares at 11 zlotys per share to up its stake to 32.9 percent.

"The reduction (of offers) will be 21.75 percent and the transaction will likely be done tomorrow," Artur Pastuszka of Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage told Reuters late on Wednesday, adding that 40 investors offered 438,995 shares.
NFI 12, which also goes by the name Piast, is one of 15 funds in Poland's mass privatisation scheme which hold stakes and manage about 500 companies.
The receiver of the bankrupt Polish insurer Westa, which had a 15.4-percent-stake in Prochnik, was among those seeking to sell shares.
